keeps.why: Claims for support are made to this office and to nobody else: the file of them is its own, from the claims already in payment when a year begins.
Each decision on a claim is this office's own paper: it pays from them, and keeps every one it has made.

issues.title: Decision on a claim for support
issues.does: Says what is decided on a claim, to the claimant. A claim granted on it is paid by the office's staff each period from then, at the sum and for the time the decision gives, while the office's standing order for paying claims is in force; a claim refused on it is not paid. It moves no money by itself.

payment.description: Which payment of the support law the claim is for, as the claim names it.

reason.description: Why not, where it is refused.

amount.description: Where granted: the sum paid each period.

every.description: Where granted: the period it is paid by.

until.description: Where granted for a time: the day the payment ends.

issues.title: Answer to a request to put something right
issues.does: Answers someone who has asked the office in writing to put something right: yes or no, and where money is owed them and paid, how much. It does nothing by itself: what puts the thing right (a payment, a repair ordered, a paper withdrawn) is done besides.

matter.description: What it is about, in the word the request uses.

granted.description: Whether it will be put right.

amount.description: Where money is owed them and paid: how much.

issues.title: Answer to a desk's notice of an application against the office
issues.does: Answers a body that has told the office of an application against it, from the office's own books: what they show is owed, whether the thing is done, whether the paper complained of was wrong. The body decides on it when the time to answer has run; with no answer it decides in default.

venue.description: The body that sent the notice.

known.description: Whether the office's books say anything of it.

owed.description: What the books show is owed the applicant (nought: nothing).

done.description: For a thing to be put right: whether it is done.

wrong.description: For a paper complained of: whether it was wrong.

statement.description: What the office says in answer, in its own words, where these do not say it (what it disputes, and why).

routines.what: Each working day the office's staff decide the claims that have waited their time, the oldest first: a claim that meets the conditions the support law states for its payment is granted, in writing, and paid each period from then until the claimant asks for it to stop, dies, leaves, or its time runs out, which the staff tell them. A claim that does not meet the conditions, or that the staff could not verify, is not refused by the staff: it is put before whoever holds the office, as a note on the office's file saying what it fails on, and decided by them on the office's decision form; a claim they grant on that form is paid by the staff like any other. A request to look at a decision again comes to the office-holder. What a claim waits for before it is decided (papers from the claimant, a confirmation from their last employer, within so many days) is the law's: the staff ask for it and the claim stays on their file until it has come or its time has run.

papers.how: decided by the support law's conditions: granted and paid if it meets them, put before the office-holder if it does not or could not be verified
a claimant's own request to stop their payment: it is stopped
